key_insight: Moderate adverse pressure gradients leave the wall-scaled attached-eddy hierarchy largely unchanged, but add outer-region energy from an embedded shear-layer-like structure that becomes increasingly important toward the log layer.
engineering_relevance: For high-Re boundary-layer design and modeling, pressure gradients mainly alter outer-region momentum transfer and variance through wall-incoherent energetic structures rather than by rewriting near-wall scaling.
method: Compared ZPG and APG boundary layers at matched friction Reynolds number near 10,000.
Used two-point hot-wire measurements to estimate the linear coherence spectrum and separate wall-coherent from wall-incoherent energy.
Used conditional averaging of PIV data to identify the structures associated with APG-induced energisation.
evidence_signal: Across two complementary datasets, the wall-coherent attached-eddy contribution remained similar, while the extra APG variance was largely incoherent with the wall and associated with outer shear-layer organization.
watch_item: The conclusions are drawn for low-to-moderate APG cases with minimal upstream history, so stronger pressure gradients or different development histories may not follow the same scaling.
paper_title: Wall-scaled eddies and embedded shear layers in high-Reynolds-number moderate adverse-pressure-gradient boundary layers
